headline: Low interaction risk: MinerU and Whisper have no shared write surfaces or default data exchange, so prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors are limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU can use an MCP server and processes document content, while Whisper only handles audio files and has no clipboard/MCP surface. There is no documented shared channel or default ingestion path between them, so prompt injection is not a default pathway; any bridge would require unusual orchestration.
conditions: IF an operator wires MinerU outputs into a prompt-consuming agent before Whisper runs, injection risk increases.
IF a shared MCP or message bus is added between the two, attacker-controlled document text can propagate.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workflows with no automatic handoff.
Disable or restrict MinerU MCP exposure unless needed.
Manually inspect any text passed from MinerU before reuse.
Use separate queues/directories for document and audio jobs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, and OCR text, but its filesystem access is read-only and Whisper only reads audio files with no network egress. The profiles show no shared workspace, OAuth principal, or outbound upload path, so a pairwise leakage route is not evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same sensitive directory, local exposure becomes possible.
IF either profile is changed to upload file contents to a third party, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Store document and audio inputs in separate directories.
Avoid placing secrets in shared working folders.
Keep network egress disabled except allowlisted MinerU endpoints.
Review any future connector that forwards file contents off-host.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Neither agent can write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, and Whisper has no network egress. MinerU's allowlisted egress does not create a shared mutable resource with Whisper, so there is no overlapping write-capability conflict in the documented profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is granted write access to the same directory, conflict risk appears.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state or locking-free git operations, contention can emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in shared environments.
Do not mount a common writable workspace.
Add external locking before any future write-enabled integration.
Run each agent in separate containers or sandboxes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted document text and structured outputs, but Whisper is an audio-speech model with no documented downstream action-taking authority. Because there is no default pipeline showing Whisper consuming MinerU outputs as authoritative instructions, cascading error is limited and would require an added orchestration step.
conditions: IF MinerU text is fed into a downstream agent that acts without verification, errors can cascade.
IF Whisper outputs are used as authoritative labels for document actions, misclassification can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a verification step between MinerU and any action-taking system.
Require human review for extracted facts before use.
Keep Whisper outputs separate from document-processing decisions.
Log provenance for any cross-agent handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced in the profiles: MinerU is open-source, private/offline, and Whisper has no network egress or special handling claims. The pair does not show PHI, EU PII, residency, or retention differences, so a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either workflow, compliance review is needed.
IF one agent is deployed under a stricter residency or retention policy than the other, mismatch risk appears.
mitigations: Document the data classes each workflow may process.
Keep regulated data out of unreviewed pipelines.
Align retention settings before deployment.
Perform a policy review if residency requirements change.
